title: Upper bound for switching failure
statement: Let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be a sign-valued Boolean function, let $k\\in\\mathbb N$, and suppose $0\\le\\delta\\le 1$. The switching-failure probability, the weighted average over random restrictions of the indicator that the restricted function has decision-tree depth at least $k$, is at most $1$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the sign cube with sign-valued output
